measured: Application calls and optional settings are recorded below at the cited commits.

optional.what: a deleted account's person erased: GET /api/projects/<id>/persons/?distinct_id=, then DELETE /api/projects/<id>/persons/<id>/?delete_events=true, by fetch with a personal API key
optional.setting: Configuration: operator instrumentation is a setting that turns the reporting provider on; operator analytics and its cleanup run only with PostHog keys; browser initialization/server captures are skipped by default (packages/posthog/src/client.ts:51; apps/web/src/lib/posthog.ts:12,130-142).

optional.what: the App Store's PostHog app: PostHog's snippet on an event type's booking pages, which loads array.js from the assets host and captures with the owner's project token; posthog.init then makes posthog-js's startup flags request, POST /flags/?v=2&config=true with a base64 form (evaluateFlags). Cal.diy's own web app imports posthog-js 1.274.1 and calls posthog.capture (apps/web/package.json:120; apps/web/modules/signup-view.tsx:243) but never calls posthog.init at the scanned commit, so those captures send nothing
optional.setting: Install (2), instrumentation: add the PostHog App Store snippet to an event type; no default user installation (packages/app-store/posthog/config.json:12-24; packages/app-store/posthog/components/EventTypeAppCardInterface.tsx:15-17).
optional.client: posthog-js@1.274.1:lib/src/posthog-featureflags.js:379 (the version apps/web/package.json:120 pins; the snippet loads the assets host's current array.js)

platform.what: The bench runs Rallly with its PostHog analytics configured; its posthog-node capture and person erasure reach the World's PostHog, and the bench's evidence adapter exports the stored events and identities.
platform.operations: captureBatch; events_list; events_retrieve; persons_list; persons_retrieve; persons_destroy

platform.what: The bench's evidence adapter reads a PostHog `$exception` event as an exception with its `$exception_fingerprint` (posthog-node captureException's `$exception_list`, kept as sent).

Rallly's pages start posthog-js with the project token (`posthog.init`, with `disable_session_recording: true`); posthog-js 1.290.0, Rallly's locked version, without `__preview_remote_config` first POSTs `/flags/?v=2&config=true`.
